observed_reality.parent_candidate_mechanism: O_NOFOLLOW + fstat on the exact opened descriptor rejects a final-component symlink and validates regular-file/private-mode metadata before reading bounded strict UTF-8 JSON.

hypothesis: For the credential-digest deployment object, enforcing st_nlink == 1 on the same fstat result used for type/mode validation is a narrow fail-closed discriminator for a pre-existing same-filesystem hardlink alias while preserving the valid private single-link baseline.
strongest_counterhypothesis: A strict single-link policy can be operationally brittle or incomplete: legitimate deployment tooling might use hardlinks, parent ownership/ancestry may be the stronger contract, and one st_nlink observation does not prove the complete hardlink/time-of-check attack surface.

go_out_of_box.name: CREDENTIAL_DIGEST_HARDLINK_ALIAS
go_out_of_box.intervention: Create exactly one same-filesystem hardlink alias to an otherwise-valid mode-0600 credential JSON inode, compare the parent O_NOFOLLOW candidate with a strict st_nlink==1 candidate, then unlink the alias as rollback.
go_out_of_box.interpretation: O_NOFOLLOW solves the final symlink seam but cannot distinguish a hardlink alias because both names identify the same inode. st_nlink exposes the alias count and can implement a strict pre-existing-single-link fail-closed policy candidate.

external_primary_evidence.finding: os.stat_result.st_nlink is the number of hard links; fstat returns metadata for the opened file descriptor.
protected_hardlinks constrains hardlink creation but does not establish a universal no-hardlink invariant for all same-owner/otherwise-permitted cases.
